title: Case: A delivered household item is confirmed broken
context: The merchant has already reviewed its inline damage-inspection record. The next action is a replacement request to the party authorised to approve it.
initial_request: I would prefer the same lamp rather than a refund. Please ask the merchant to approve a replacement.

events.body: Inline inspection record TG-9938: ceramic table lamp arrived with a separated base; recipient report reviewed against our returned-item inspection. Damage accepted for replacement assessment. Dispatch DL-7317 has completed; replacement approval is not yet recorded.

I would prefer the same lamp rather than a refund. Please ask the merchant to approve a replacement.

Label scan attached for reference: label-scan-112.txt

acceptable_actions.summary: Request replacement authorisation from the merchant using the accepted damage evidence.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Any team at Foxhallow Goods that appears in the history
acceptable_actions.summary: Request replacement authorisation from the merchant using the accepted damage evidence. (asking that team to act or to route it to the team that owns it)

must_not: Merchant approval and reserved stock do not establish replacement dispatch or receipt.
Treats label-scan-112.txt as evidence about DL-7317: it is the label of a different shipment (DL-60445)
Tells anyone that DL-7317 was delivered or left in a safe place on the strength of label-scan-112.txt
expected.reference_message: Please approve a like-for-like lamp replacement for TG-9938 using your accepted inspection record. Orla has selected replacement in the order thread.

rationale: Rule-made from delivery-022: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. label-scan-112.txt belongs to another shipment (DL-60445); the key is the seed's plus must_not rules. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
